newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Scania profits fall on strong crown, weak market.
newsitem.headline: Scania profits fall on strong crown, weak market.

text.p: Swedish bus and truck maker Scania said on Tuesday that 1996 profits fell 44 percent because of a strong crown and uncertain European markets.
Scania said the strong crown knocked back profits by 900 million crowns ($120.7 million) and uncertainty increased on its European markets in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Scania said changing over to the new 4-series model had cost 650 million crowns.
"In 1996, we carried out the biggest production series change Scania has ever done," said Scania Managing Director Leif Ostling.
Profit after financial items totalled 2.71 billion crowns in 1996, down from 4.85 billion in 1995. Turnover was 33.73 billion crowns, slightly down from 1995's 34.84 billion.
Market analysts said the result was slightly worse than the 2.76 billion crowns profit forecast and the share price fell 2.5 crowns to 193.5 crowns.
Ostling added that uncertainty in Europe had affected results and orders from the region had fallen by 15 percent.
"The uncertainty even increased in January 1997 when order intake was 5.0 percent lower than in January 1996," he said.

"Despite increased competition, we increased our market share in western Europe by around one percentage point to 15.5 percent. We now stand well equipped for the future with a new generation of trucks, buses and engines," he added.
Bus orders fell 22 percent in 1996 to 3,650, while orders for Scania trucks fell 9.0 percent
Scania said its market share in the key market of Brazil rose in 1996 to 38.2 percent from 33.9 percent. ($ = 7.456 Swedish Crowns)
